'''Vadim Veniaminovich Brazhkin''' (born [[October 24]], 1961, in [[Zlatoust]]) is a Russian physicist, Academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences (since 2016), and [[Doctor of Sciences|Doctor of Physical and Mathematical Sciences]]. He is Director of the [[Institute for High Pressure Physics|Institute of High Pressure Physics of the Russian Academy of Sciences]]. He specializes in the physics of [[Phase transition|phase transitions]] and [[Disordered media physics|disordered media]], [[high-pressure physics]], and [[condensed matter physics]]. He has authored approximately 500 scientific publications and has been cited over 10,000 times. His [[H-index|''h''-index]] is 43 (WOS), 53 (Google Scholar), and 44 (Scopus).

== Early life and education ==
Vadim Veniaminovich Brazhkin was born on October 24, 1961 in [[Zlatoust]]. In 1978, he entered the Faculty of Physics and Energy Problems at Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology ([[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology|MIPT]]). After graduating from the faculty, he entered graduate school at MIPT. In 1987, he defended his PhD dissertation.

==Career==
He began working at the Institute for High Pressure Physics, Russian Academy of Sciences ([[Institute for High Pressure Physics|HPPI RAS]]), located in [[Troitsk, Moscow]]. In 1996 he defended his doctoral dissertation. Since 1993, he has held the position of Deputy Director of the Institute of High Pressure Physics of the Russian Academy of Sciences. In 2016, he became HPPI RAS's Director.
In 2011, he was elected as a [[Corresponding Member]] of the Russian Academy of Sciences.
In 2016, he was elected as an academician of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Brazhkin discovered and studied a new phenomenon: [[Phase transformation|phase transformations]] in [[Melting|melts]] of [[Elementary substance|elementary substances]] and simple compounds under [[pressure]]. He established that the transformations are accompanied by sharp changes in the structure and properties of the liquid; in a number of substances, [[dielectric]] metal transitions are realized.{{Clarify|date=November 2026}} Under the leadership of Brazhkin, a series of fundamental works on the study of sharp and blurred [[Structural transformation|structural transformations]] in glasses and amorphous solids was also carried out. He discovered the first logarithmic kinetics of such transformations for a number of non-glass-forming molecular compounds (<math>AsS, P_4Se_3, P_4S_3</math>) by [[quenching]] the melt at [[High pressure|high pressures]].

While studying the phenomenon of solid-phase [[Amorphous solid|amorphization]] of crystals under pressure, Brazhkin was the first to obtain bulk phases of amorphous [[tetrahedral]] [[semiconductors]]. He experimentally established that solid-phase amorphization is caused by a decrease in the [[shear moduli]] of the corresponding [[Crystal lattice|crystal lattices]].

Brazhkin has completed a large series of studies on the effect of high pressure on the [[viscosity]] of liquids. It has been established that the viscosity of many [[Oxide|liquid oxides]] and [[Chalcogenide|chalcogenides]] undergoing phase transformations drops sharply under compression by several orders of magnitude.
	Brazhkin showed that most molecular compounds based on light elements are thermodynamically metastable phases. At high pressures, these substances undergo irreversible transformations into [[polymerized]] states.
	Research into transformations in [[Melting|liquids]] and [[Glass transition|glasses]], conducted by Brazhkin since 1986, has effectively led to the creation of a new direction in condensed matter physics. Brazhkin was co-chairman of the first major international meeting (2001) devoted to phase transformations in disordered media.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ссыока |url=http://www.hppi.troitsk.ru/meetings/Nato/nato.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427095830/http://www.hppi.troitsk.ru/meetings/Nato/nato.htm |archive-date=2017-04-27 |access-date=2017-02-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=2021-10-01 |title=Vadim Veniaminovich Brazhkin (on his 60th birthday) |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.3367/UFNe.2021.09.039058 |url-status=live |journal=Physics-Uspekhi |language=en |publisher=[[IOP Publishing]] |volume=64 |issue=10 |pages=1067 |doi=10.3367/UFNe.2021.09.039058 |issn=1063-7869 |url-access=subscription |access-date=13 November 2026 |via=[[IOPscience]]}}</ref>

	In recent years, Brazhkin's research has shifted toward studying the structure and dynamics of [[Supercritical fluid|supercritical fluids]]. Brazhkin and his colleagues have obtained significant results in theoretical and experimental studies of fluids. They have established that an analog of the [[Liquidus and solidus|liquid-gas line]], in terms of the excitation spectrum in fluids, exists at any pressure. These results demonstrate the need for a significant revision of the "classical" view of the nature of the [[Liquid#Prediction of liquid properties|liquid state]].

He is a member of the [[July 1st Club]].

==Awards and honours==
* On February 5, 2024, he was awarded the [[Medal of the Order "For Merit to the Fatherland"]], 2nd class, for his great contribution to the development of Russian science, many years of fruitful work,{{Weasel inline|date=November 2026}} and in connection with the 300th anniversary of the founding of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 5 февраля 2024 года № 91 «О награждении государственными наградами Российской Федерации» |url=http://publication.pravo.gov.ru/document/0001202402050015?index=10 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240206114218/http://publication.pravo.gov.ru/document/0001202402050015?index=10 |archive-date=2024-02-06 |access-date=2024-02-06}}</ref>
* Laureate of the Russian Academy of Sciences Prize named after A. G. Stoletova ([http://www.ras.ru/viewnumbereddoc.aspx?id=710f954e-4c2c-49a4-9c8b-5d301b6cde86&_Language=ru 2017])
* Laureate of the People's Prize "Bright Past" ([https://www.fondmityaev.ru/projects/12/ 2019])
